items.title: 11.7.2 Carbocation stability and the inductive effect of alkyl groups (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 11.7.2 with Figure 11.11, printed pages 258-259.

blocks.text: Carbocation aik alkyl group hai jis ke kisi aik carbon atom par aik positive charge hota hai. Carbocations ki yeh types (qismein) hain.

items: Jo carbocation (positive carbon) sirf H se jura ho use methyl carbocation kehte hain.
Agar positive carbon aik C ya alkyl group se jura ho to use primary (1º) carbocation kehte hain.
Agar woh seedha 2 carbons (alkyl groups) se jura ho to use secondary (2º) carbocation kehte hain.
Agar woh seedha 3 carbons (alkyl groups) se jura ho to use tertiary (3º) carbocation kehte hain.

blocks.text: Carbocation ki stability mein alkyl groups ka inductive effect bara role (kirdar) ada karta hai.

blocks.title: Inductive effect
blocks.text: Paas wale groups ya atoms ke electrons kheenchne (withdraw) ya dene (donate) ke asar se σ bond ka polar ho jana (electrons ka aik taraf khisak jana) inductive effect kehlata hai.

Alkyl groups ka inductive effect thora electron dene wala hota hai. Electron dene wali species ka inductive effect positive (+I) kehlata hai, jabke electron kheenchne wali species, jaise halogen atom, ka inductive effect negative (−I) hota hai.

Positive carbon se jure alkyl groups electron dene wale groups hain. Carbon par positive charge ki wajah se carbocation electrophile hai. Inductive effect bonds par arrowheads (teer ke sire) se dikhaya jata hai, jo batate hain ke alkyl groups electrons ko positive carbon ki taraf dhakel rahe hain.

blocks.alt: Ek row mein chaar carbocations, darmiyan mein 'kam se' ke nishan: methyl (teen H wala C+), 1 degree (ek R, R-C bond par arrowhead C+ ki taraf), 2 degree (do R) aur 3 degree (teen R); har ek ke neeche electron dene wale alkyl groups ki number (tadaad). Neeche red teer: Stability increases.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.11: Inductive effect aur carbocation ki stability (kitab ki Figure 11.11 jaisa original diagram).

blocks.title: Diagram ko samjhein
blocks.text: Left se right positive carbon par alkyl groups (R) ki number 0, 1, 2, 3 hai. Har R ka teer electrons ko C⁺ ki taraf dhakelta hai. Jitne zyada R, utna zyada charge phailta hai aur carbocation utna stable: methyl < 1º < 2º < 3º.

Is ka result (nateeja) yeh hai ke carbocation par positive charge kam ho jata hai aur woh energy ke hisaab se zyada stable ho jata hai. Alkyl groups ke +I effect ki wajah se carbocation ki stability alkyl groups barhne ke saath barhti hai. Is ka matlab hai ke tertiary carbocation sab se zyada stable hai, kyunke us par teen electron dene wale alkyl groups hain (Figure 11.11).

blocks.prompt: Carbocation stability ki tarteeb tertiary > secondary > primary kyun hai (Quick Check 11.6b; exercise Q.2i)?
blocks.explanation: Positive carbon se jura har alkyl group σ bonds ke zariye electrons ko us ki taraf dhakelta hai (+I effect) aur positive charge ko phaila kar kam karta hai. Teen alkyl groups do se zyada electrons dete hain aur do aik se zyada; is liye tertiary ion par charge sab se zyada phaila hua hai aur us ki energy sab se kam hai.

items: Carbocation: C⁺ wala alkyl group; C⁺ se jure carbons ki number se methyl, primary, secondary, tertiary.
Alkyl groups +I (electron dene wale), halogens −I (kheenchne wale); +I charge phailata hai, is liye stability 3º > 2º > 1º > methyl.
